thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: elevated packet loss observed from edge-pop us-west2-cdn -> last-mile ISP across multiple customers (start=2026-03-15T02:12Z). Affected prefixes: 52.1.3.0/24, 52.1.4.0/24. Metric: 30-60% packet loss, high retransmits. Paging oncall-net

Avery: Acked. Oncall-net here, pulling BGP/RIB and perf graphs. Starting correlation with provider telemetry.

Jon: I see the same in Datadog for requests routed through us-west2 edge. 502s spike for API frontends, cache hit-rate fell ~18%.

Maria: From edge telemetry: egress queues spiking for those prefixes, packet drops at our peering egress. Lastmile jitter aligns with TransitOne peer ASN 64512.

Avery: Can someone open a provider ticket? I'll try temporary egress steering to alternate peers.

Kevin: Filed contact ticket with TransitOne: T1-45891. Support says they see partial degradation on their handoff to ISP. ETA unknown.

Erik: Adding routing note — we've got healthy capacity to push via EdgePeer-B and CloudBackhaul. I'll prep RIB changes: set local-preference higher for alternate next-hops for prefixes 52.1.3.0/24 and 52.1.4.0/24.

Avery: Applying emergency policy to prefer-edgepeer-b for affected prefixes now. Command run: 
```
# route-policy temporary-steer
set local-preference 200 for 52.1.3.0/24 52.1.4.0/24
commit
```

Avery: Pushed, waiting for propagation.

Jon: Seeing error rate drop in the first 60s for some clients. Overall latency still elevated for long-lived connections.

Maria: We should also reduce TTLs on CDN config to force re-resolve where DNS-based steering can help. Lowering origin TTLs to 30s for affected edge routes.

Kevin: Notifying CS and 1 cust with active degraded sessions (acct: enterprise-beta). Drafting banner: "We are mitigating a regional edge connectivity issue in US-WEST. Some requests may retry or fail; engineers are actively rerouting traffic."

Avery: Quick note — enabling prefix-specific fallback so requests that still hit the flaky path will fallback to nearest healthy POP via latency routing. Turning on failover policy now.

devops-bot: Deploy pipeline job to update routing policies queued: job #rte-2026-1939. No service restarts required.

Avery: Canary checks look good: packet loss down to ~5-8% on alternate path. Some customers still get intermittent failures due to TCP session drops — need to advise customers to retry or reconnect.

Jon: Also seeing degraded websocket connections — we have a short-term plan: 1) steer new connections away; 2) consider forcing rolling restart of connection proxies in us-west2 if sessions remain stuck. Prefer #1 for now.

Maria: I pushed a cache-warm request for critical static assets and adjusted origin failover weight to 0.8 for EdgePeer-B to favor warmed caches.

Erik: BGP adjacencies stable. TransitOne reports they're investigating an ISP handoff upstream; they applied a partial mitigation at 02:28Z. We should keep their ticket open.

Kevin: Sent customer advisory to affected customers list. Copy of message: "We are aware of increased errors and retries for requests routed through our US-WEST edge. Engineers have rerouted traffic and are monitoring. No action required from you unless you continue to see errors; please contact support with timestamps."

Avery: Status update for execs: mitigation in place, primary impact window 02:12–02:30 UTC, residual elevated errors for another ~20m. Declaring incident-level P2 for now while we monitor.

Jon: Agree with P2. Logging postmortem flag. We'll escalate to P1 if broader customer impact increases.

Maria: Observability note: capturing packet captures and interface counters from affected egress nodes to attach to provider ticket. Uploading to T1-45891 now.

Avery: Handing off to overnight oncall in 45m. I'll collate timeline and current state for handoff. Handoff checklist: current egress policy, TransitOne ticket ID, cache TTL changes, customer advisory link.

Erik: Quick test command I ran: `curl -I https://us-west2-edge.example.com/static/logo.png --resolve us-west2-edge.example.com:443:52.1.3.14` — returned 502 when hitting original path, 200 after steer. Sharing in case useful for SRE debugging.

devops-bot: Monitoring alert thresholds adjusted to avoid duplicate paging during propagation window.

Kevin: CS updated. Two paying customers reported timeouts; both acknowledged the notice and will monitor.

Avery: Current mitigation summary: 1) emergency local-pref steer to EdgePeer-B (done), 2) TTL lowered for CDN DNS on affected routes (done), 3) cache-warm for critical assets (done), 4) provider ticket open (T1-45891), 5) watching for error spikes/502 rates.

Jon: If TransitOne confirms upstream stability, we'll revert steer and TTLs after 30m stable.

Maria: I'll prepare a short playbook fragment for this failure mode: BGP peer handoff congestion — steps + commands + traffic steering entries.

Avery: Handoff note for next oncall: if errors climb >15% for 5m, escalate to Eng-Network and declare P1. Keep TransitOne ticket active and request root-cause report.

Erik: We should consider a follow-up action item: test failover to CloudBackhaul in staging for these prefixes and run a scheduled BGP failover drill. Adding to infra backlog.

Avery: Ok folks — still monitoring. If anything changes I'll ping here. :thumbsup:

Kevin: Thanks — closing customer advisory loop for now.

devops-bot: Alert: error-rate returned to baseline at 02:40Z. Incident marked as recovered by automated monitoring but thread remains open for handoff.

Avery: Confirmed recovery. Last observed residual errors cleared by 02:39Z. Will finalize notes and start a short postmortem doc tomorrow.

Jon: Reassigning follow-ups: `infra#bgp-failover-drill`, `postmortem#1939993333`.

Avery: Handoff to Erik for overnight 02:45Z–10:45Z. Erik please ack.

Erik: Acked. I'll own the watch and reopen if we see any regression.

Avery: Thanks everyone. Closing the live mitigation thread — postmortem + timeline to follow.
